name: mega65-dev
description: Systems-level MEGA65 development: the 45GS02 memory model, the MAP register and banking, 28-bit addressing and DMAgic, MEGA65/C65 hardware registers, the KERNAL jump table and its zero-page and Z-register hazards, the Hyppo hypervisor traps, and emulator-based testing under xemu. Toolchain-neutral, with claims checked against mega65-core, the MEGA65 Book, and the ROM sources.

interface.shortDescription: Systems-level MEGA65 development: memory model, MAP and banking, hardware registers, KERNAL, hypervisor.
interface.longDescription: Reusable, evidence-backed guidance for programming the MEGA65 at the systems level. Covers the 28-bit address space and Chip/Attic RAM map, the four address-translation layers and their precedence, the MAP register including the extended 28-bit form and its interrupt semantics, banking patterns and their failure modes, hardware registers for the VIC-IV, DMAgic, MATH unit and SD/floppy controller together with a lookup recipe for the VHDL-generated register master list, the KERNAL jump table with its MAP preconditions and Z-register hazards, the Hyppo hypervisor trap interface, and scripted testing under the xemu emulator including self-checking harnesses and known emulator-versus-hardware divergences. Examples are plain 45GS02 assembly; no toolchain is assumed. Sources are the mega65-core VHDL, the MEGA65 Book, and the ROM sources, in that order of authority.

Use mega65-dev to check whether this KERNAL call is safe to make from banked code.
Use mega65-dev to set up a scripted xemu test for this program.
